6. Why does Java use UTF-16 instead of ASCII for char representation?
ASCII is limited to 128 English symbols. It is therefore not sufficient for applications that need to represent characters from many different languages.
Java was designed for applications that could be used internationally. Therefore, it uses a character representation capable of supporting a much larger set of characters.

A character has a numeric character code. Therefore, when a character participates in an arithmetic expression, its numeric value is used.

12. What is type casting in Java?
Type casting is the process of converting data from one data type to another data type.
Primitive type casting has two forms:
